solutions.question: 2(c)
solutions.latex:
$P(6)=\dfrac16$, $P(\text{not }6)=\dfrac56$.

Tree diagram: at each roll the game ends with probability $\dfrac16$ or continues (not 6) with probability $\dfrac56$.

$$P(\text{ends before 4th roll})=\dfrac16+\dfrac56\times\dfrac16+\dfrac56\times\dfrac56\times\dfrac16=\dfrac16+\dfrac56\times\dfrac16+\left(\dfrac56\right)^2\times\dfrac16$$

Alternate solution: $P(\text{win 1st roll})=\dfrac16$, $P(\text{win 2nd roll})=\dfrac56\times\dfrac16$, $P(\text{win 3rd roll})=\dfrac56\times\dfrac56\times\dfrac16$; add these.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution; 1: drawing tree diagram or setting up correct reasoning

solutions.question: 2(c)
solutions.latex:
$$P(\text{ends before }n\text{th roll})=\left(\dfrac56\right)^0\dfrac16+\left(\dfrac56\right)^1\dfrac16+\dots+\left(\dfrac56\right)^{n-2}\dfrac16$$

Geometric series with $a=\dfrac16$, $r=\dfrac56$ and $n-1$ terms:

$$S_{n-1}=\dfrac{\frac16\left(1-\left(\frac56\right)^{n-1}\right)}{1-\frac56}=1-\left(\dfrac56\right)^{n-1}$$

$0.9=1-\left(\dfrac56\right)^{n-1}$, so $\left(\dfrac56\right)^{n-1}=0.1$.

$(n-1)\log\dfrac56=\log 0.1$, so $n-1=\dfrac{\log0.1}{\log\frac56}=12.629\dots$, $n=13.629\dots$

Smallest value of $n$ is $14$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: correct simplified equation to solve; 1: establishing series for probability of ending before $n$th roll

solutions.question: 4(d)
solutions.latex:
Probabilities sum to 1: $r+r^2+r^3+\dots+r^{n-1}+r^n=1$.

Geometric series with $a=r$, ratio $r$, $n$ terms:

$$S_n=\dfrac{a(r^n-1)}{r-1}=\dfrac{r(r^n-1)}{r-1}=1$$

$r^{n+1}-r=r-1$, so $r^{n+1}=2r-1$. $\quad(1)$

$$E(X)=\sum xP(X=x)=r\cdot r^n+r^2\cdot r^{n-1}+r^3\cdot r^{n-2}+\dots+r^n\cdot r=r^{n+1}+r^{n+1}+\dots+r^{n+1}=nr^{n+1}$$

From (1), $nr^{n+1}=n(2r-1)$, as required.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: using sum of geometric series to establish $r^{n+1}=2r-1$ OR determining $E(X)=nr^{n+1}$; 1: setting up series equal to 1
